outcome: feeding practices of infants and young children
cohort: The study included 280 mothers of infants and young children aged 0-23 months living in Pokhara Metropolitan City.
finding: The study concluded that the feeding practices for the majority of infants and young children in Pokhara were not adequate according to WHO and UNICEF standards, with only 32.3% of children 0-5 months appropriately breastfed and 41.8% of children 6-23 months having appropriate complementary feeding practices.
mod_finding: Children delivered by normal vaginal delivery were more likely to have appropriate breastfeeding practices than those delivered by caesarean section.
cross-section timing: Mothers of infants and young children aged 0-23 months were interviewed at the time of the study.
